findings.title: No MX records
findings.detail: The domain has no MX records, so it may not receive email. This is not always a problem. Some domains are only used for a website.

findings.title: SPF record ends with -all
findings.detail: The SPF record exists and tells mail servers to reject (-all) or mark as suspicious (~all) email from servers that are not on the list.

findings.title: SPF needs 0 DNS lookups (limit is 10)
findings.detail: The SPF record stays inside the limit of 10 DNS lookups.

findings.title: DMARC policy is p=reject
findings.detail: DMARC tells mail servers to send failing email to spam (quarantine) or to refuse it (reject).

findings.title: DMARC has no reporting address (rua)
findings.detail: The DMARC record has no rua= tag. The owner gets no reports, so they cannot see if someone is sending fake email in their name.

findings.title: No DKIM key found for common selectors
findings.detail: I did not find a DKIM key for the common selectors I tried. This does NOT prove DKIM is missing. DKIM selectors can have any name, and there is no way to list them from DNS.
findings.evidence: Selectors tried: google, selector1, selector2, default, k1

findings.title: No CAA record
findings.detail: The domain does not limit which certificate authorities may issue certificates for it. Any public authority could issue one.

findings.title: Website answers on HTTPS
findings.detail: https://example.com/ loaded over an encrypted connection.

findings.title: HTTP does not redirect to HTTPS
findings.detail: The plain http:// site loads without moving visitors to https://. Anyone on the same network could read or change that traffic.

findings.title: No Strict-Transport-Security header
findings.detail: Browsers are not told to always use HTTPS, so a first visit over plain HTTP could be intercepted.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header
findings.detail: The site does not limit which scripts and content browsers may load.

findings.title: No X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
findings.detail: Browsers may guess file types. An attacker can sometimes use this to run a file as a script.

findings.title: No frame protection
findings.detail: Other sites could show this site inside a hidden frame and trick users into clicking on it (clickjacking).

findings.title: No Referrer-Policy header
findings.detail: The site does not set a Referrer-Policy, so browsers use their own default. Older browsers may share full page addresses with other sites.

findings.title: No security.txt
findings.detail: There is no /.well-known/security.txt file, so it is not clear how to report a security problem to this company.

findings.title: Certificate is valid for 63 more days
findings.detail: The website certificate is valid and not close to running out.

findings.title: Server uses TLSv1.3
findings.detail: The server chose a current version of TLS.

questions: Your DMARC record has no reporting address. Who would notice if someone started sending fake email in your name?
I could not find a DKIM key with common names. Do you sign outgoing email with DKIM, and which selector do you use?
Your website still loads over plain HTTP. Can you redirect all visitors to HTTPS?
Your website does not send Strict-Transport-Security. Can you add it?
Your website has no Content-Security-Policy. Is one planned?
Your website does not stop other sites from showing it in a frame. Can you add X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors?
Your website does not send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Can you add it?
Your website does not set a Referrer-Policy. Can you add one?
Your domain has no CAA record. Would you consider adding one for the certificate authorities you use?
There is no security.txt on your website. How should someone report a security problem to you?
